facts.claim: Children with obesity often have deficiencies in essential macro- and micronutrients despite having a high caloric intake.
facts.quote: Despite high caloric intake, children with obesity often display deficiencies in essential macro- and micronutrients that impair growth, metabolic regulation, and long-term health.

facts.claim: Diets rich in fiber, fruit, vegetables, and anti-inflammatory nutrients and low in saturated fats seem to promote better sleep quality.
facts.quote: Diets rich in fiber, fruit, vegetables, and anti-inflammatory nutrients and low in saturated fats seem to promote better sleep quality.

facts.claim: There is a lack of data from clinical studies in children of various ages consuming different levels of dietary fiber to support assumptions about its effects.
facts.quote: However, there is a lack of data from clinical studies in children of various ages consuming different levels of dietary fiber to support such assumptions.

facts.claim: Clinical trial outcomes for dietary fiber in children vary according to fiber type, dosage, duration of intervention, and diagnostic criteria.
facts.quote: However, clinical trial outcomes remain inconsistent, varying according to fiber type, dosage, duration of intervention, and diagnostic criteria.

facts.claim: Most children around the world eat amounts of dietary fiber that are well below recommended levels.
facts.quote: Dietary fiber plays a central role in pediatric gastrointestinal health; however, most children worldwide consume amounts well below recommended levels.

facts.claim: Explicit statewide support for plant-based or vegetarian school meals remains rare in the United States.
facts.quote: Explicit statewide support for plant-based or vegetarian school meals remains rare in the United States.

research.angle: While children often consume low fiber and high calories, there is a lack of clinical data to confirm exactly how specific fiber-to-calorie ratios in school meals affect insulin resistance.
research.verdict: The sources confirm that children often have low fiber intake and that school programs lack plant-based policies, but they do not provide specific data on the fiber-to-calorie ratios of government-subsidized meals.
research.caveat: Most evidence regarding the specific health effects of fiber in children is currently inconsistent or lacking from high-quality clinical trials.
